what: A family's draws before the fight, made each unpaused frame of the opening before the appear's bit 0, paired from the opening's end: where BN4's made more of a key's than BN6's, the battle is run again with BN6's k-th setup draw of the key given BN4's (k + N)-th, BN4's first N left without a twin (tools/xdiff_bn4.py opening_skips, the spec's setupskip=KEY:N, src/dev/xdiff_events.c replay_setup). N is bounded, never the gap of the counts: it must equal BN4's draws of the key in the two unpaused frames BN6's opening has no twin of, read from BN4's trace by frame (twinless_draws: the family object's init frame, its spawn's, and the frame before the appear's bit 0, the frame before BN4_APPEAR's step 0 plays its sound as it sees the bit); where the gap is any other number (a draw of BN6's dropped or added), nothing is paired so and the spec runs as it is, failing where the family's state parts. BN6's count of them must be the same in both runs, else INCONCLUSIVE. Every other setup draw keeps the reference's k-th (Shrimpy's and Spikey's one draw in their init, the same count in both).
why: The engines' openings differ by two unpaused frames before the appear's bit 0, the two the opening's alignment (align, BN6's battle opening a frame longer) and the battle's offset (allowed, lag 1) name: BN4's family runs its update in its init's frame (its type routine's init ends in the update) and BN4 sets bit 0 18 frames after the init, BN6 17, BN6's hook 3 running from the frame after the init. A family whose update's own step draws every such frame draws two more in BN4: MagTect's shake (BN4 0x080BF064, entered as hook 3 from 0x080BEBF6: unless the battle is paused, 0x08007948, or the can-move check's third form says not, 0x0800AD7E, and while its +0x20 is a multiple of 4, its offsets +0x36 and +0x3E moved to a random pair of its table's bytes, kept at +0x64 and +0x68) draws at BN4's frames 132-149 (18, the first in its init's frame) and BN6's 72-87 (16) in magtect_v1, the same counts in v2 and v3. Each shake sets its offsets from that draw alone (+0x64 the new byte, +0x36 moved by new less old), so the state the fight begins with is the last draw's: paired k-th with k-th, BN6's last takes BN4's sixteenth number where BN4's last took its eighteenth (magtect_v1 FAIL at t1 on +0x36, +0x64 and +0x9C); paired from the opening's end, BN6's sixteen take BN4's last sixteen, the frames before bit 0 the same steps of the appear's wait in both. Not the family's code: its copy runs BN4's shake whole, the engine deciding how many frames it runs before the fight.
